label: The two years since Julia's death: Helen's life is lonelier than ever
quote: Two years have passed since then

label: Many years ago: Helen comes to know Percy Armitage
quote: whom I have known for many years

label: A month ago: Percy Armitage asks Helen to marry him
quote: A month ago, however, a dear friend

label: Since the proposal: Dr. Roylott offers no opposition to the match
quote: My stepfather has offered no opposition to the match

label: Two days ago: repairs are started in the west wing
quote: Two days ago some repairs were started

label: Since the repairs began: the wall of Helen's bedroom is pierced
quote: my bedroom wall has been pierced

label: Since the repairs began: Helen moves into the room in which her sister died
quote: I have had to move into the chamber in which my sister died

label: Last night: Helen lies awake in her sister's bed, thinking of her fate
quote: as I lay awake

label: Last night: Helen hears the low whistle in the silence of the night
quote: I suddenly heard in the silence of the night the low whistle

label: Last night: Helen springs up and lights the lamp, and sees nothing in the room
quote: I sprang up and lit the lamp

label: Last night: too shaken to go back to bed, Helen dresses
quote: so I dressed

labels.label: That morning, early: the lady starts out
That morning, before six: the lady starts from home
That morning, before six, as soon as it is daylight: Helen slips out of the house

note: Holmes infers it at ¶14; she gives the hour at ¶17 and the manner at ¶67 ("as soon as it was daylight I slipped down").

label: That morning: Helen gets a dog-cart at the Crown Inn
quote: got a dog-cart at the Crown Inn

labels.label: That morning: the lady's drive in a dog-cart, along heavy roads
That morning: Helen drives from the Crown Inn to Leatherhead in a dog-cart
In a month or six weeks: the lady expects to be married
In the course of the spring, in a month or six weeks: Helen is to marry Percy Armitage

label: That morning: Helen tells of the two years since and of last night
quote: Two years have passed since then

label: That morning: Holmes asks Helen whether she has told him all
quote: But have you told me all?

label: That morning: Helen answers that she has told all
quote: Yes, all.

label: That morning: Holmes tells Helen she is screening her stepfather
quote: You are screening your stepfather

label: Some time before she came: five livid marks of a hand are left on Helen's wrist
quote: Five little livid spots, the marks of four fingers and a thumb
note: The text does not say when; the marks are on her wrist when she sits in Baker Street.

label: That morning: Holmes pushes back the lace at Helen's wrist and shows the marks
quote: Holmes pushed back the frill of black lace

label: That morning: Holmes says Helen has been cruelly used
quote: You have been cruelly used

label: That morning: Helen covers her wrist and says he is a hard man
quote: covered over her injured wrist

label: That morning: a long silence, while Holmes stares into the fire
quote: There was a long silence

label: That morning: Holmes asks whether they could see over the rooms at Stoke Moran unknown to her stepfather
quote: would it be possible for us to see over these rooms

label: Before Helen left home: Dr. Roylott speaks of coming into town to-day
quote: he spoke of coming into town to-day

label: By now: there is a housekeeper at Stoke Moran
quote: We have a housekeeper now

label: That morning: Helen answers that her stepfather will probably be away all day
quote: It is probable that he will be away all day

label: To-day: Dr. Roylott is expected to be in town on important business
quote: coming into town to-day upon some most important business
note: What Helen expects; the text does not order it against the talk in Baker Street.

label: That morning: Holmes asks Watson about the trip, and Watson agrees
quote: You are not averse to this trip, Watson?

label: That morning: Holmes says they will both come and asks what Helen will do
quote: Then we shall both come

label: That morning: Helen says she will do some things in town and return by the twelve o'clock train
quote: I shall return by the twelve o’clock train

label: That morning: Holmes tells Helen to expect them early in the afternoon, and offers breakfast
quote: you may expect us early in the afternoon

label: That morning: Helen declines breakfast and says her heart is lightened
quote: No, I must go

label: That morning: Helen drops her veil and leaves the room
quote: glided from the room

label: To-day: Helen means to do one or two things in town
quote: I have one or two things which I would wish to do
note: What she intends; it has not happened by the end of this scene.

label: To-day, twelve o'clock: Helen means to return by train
quote: the twelve o’clock train

label: To-day: Helen means to be back at Stoke Moran before the visit
quote: so as to be there in time for your coming

label: To-day: Holmes has some small business matters to attend to
quote: I have myself some small business matters to attend to
note: What he intends; he gives it as the reason for coming only in the afternoon.

labels.label: To-day: a possible visit to Stoke Moran
To-day: Holmes and Watson are to come to Stoke Moran
To-day, early in the afternoon: Holmes and Watson are to come to Stoke Moran

label: To-day: a possible visit to Stoke Moran
quote: If we were to come to Stoke Moran to-day
note: Planned; it has not happened by the end of this scene.

label: That morning: Holmes asks Watson what he thinks of it all
quote: And what do you think of it all, Watson?

label: That morning: Watson reasons that the sister must have been alone
quote: her sister must have been undoubtedly alone

label: That morning: Holmes asks what becomes of the whistles and the dying words, and Watson cannot think
quote: What becomes, then, of these nocturnal whistles

label: That morning: Holmes puts together the whistles, the gipsies, the band and the clang
quote: I think that there is good ground to think

label: That morning: Watson asks what the gipsies did, and Holmes cannot imagine
quote: But what, then, did the gipsies do?

label: That morning: Watson sees many objections to the theory
quote: I see many objections to any such theory

label: That morning: Holmes agrees, and says that is why they are going to Stoke Moran
quote: It is precisely for that reason that we are going to Stoke Moran this day

label: That morning: Holmes breaks off with an exclamation
quote: But what in the name of the devil!
